body:
I need to preface this by saying that I am prescribed Vyvanse, 50mg, for ADHD, and I had taken the Vyvanse maybe 9-10 hours prior. It was still working, though it was on the tail end of effectiveness but definitely still active.
I recently got a factory job, and the daily aches and pains accumulate. I have always stayed away from opiates due to a family member falling into addiction, but one night after work at a smoke shop, after mentioning my aches and pains to the guy at the register, I was recommended 7-OH as a way to numb the pain. I decided to give it a shot after getting home.
I got a 14mg pill of 7-OH and decided to give myself half a dose being the first time. I had done zero research into 7-OH but I had done kratom many times years prior, and I assumed it would be similar. I broke the pill in half and washed it down with plenty of water. I did not consume it sublingually.
Maybe 15 minutes passed, and then it hit me all at once. I heard ringing in my ears and I felt my blood pressure immediately drop. I felt light and cold in the face, my body felt weak, my heart started pounding irregularly, I had extreme dizziness, and there were several moments where the strength in my legs just gave out and I found myself on the floor.
It was then I remembered the adage of never mixing uppers and downers.
I was so foggy, it was hard to think and my heart kept feeling like it was struggling to beat quickly, like it was running in place while also being held back; the sensation was panic-inducing and indescribably uncomfortable. I did not seek medical help because of mental health struggles I had at the time, instead resigning myself to whatever was going to happen.
I kept breathing deeply, trying to slow my heart down or get it to beat regularly. After about an hour of controlled breathing and panic, the cardiac effects began to wear off.
After about an hour of controlled breathing and panic, the cardiac effects began to wear off.
My heart no longer palpitated or felt irregular. I was left feeling dizzy and deflated. The headspace was that of dissociated anxiety as I kept worrying that I was going to die from the combination, but I remained as calm as I could be.
I hopped in a hot shower for maybe 30 minutes, which helped the anxiety greatly, but the fogginess and general weakness remained. Looking back I am incredibly lucky that I did not fall in the shower.
I ended up falling asleep 3 hours after dosing myself, and I woke up the next day feeling fine. No palpitations, no weakness, and no fogginess that I can remember.
I am afraid to think what would have happened if I had taken the full dose.
I gave myself the second half of the dose that following day, not taking my Vyvanse, and the experience was relaxing and pleasant. I still felt deflated, but the palpitations and dizziness were absent. I am not an opiate connoisseur, so I don't know what to compare it to. The last time I had an opiate was codeine for pneumonia, and I barely remember how that felt through the sickness.
My main takeaway is to never ever mix amphetamines with things that act like opiates. The experience was frightening. I do plan to take 7-OH again, but making sure not to take it while any stimulants are still actively working in my system.
